Past performance enters as a variable factor, but only when sufficient data is available—otherwise it is excluded. This introduces a regime-switching mechanism in GSI’s Bayesian framework. Ownership popularity acts as a negative feedback loop, increasing salary to reduce selection bias—a form of incentive design. The interplay between these three primitives creates a dualistic structure: one layer for deterministic baseline (threshold), another for probabilistic performance (data-dependent), and a third for behavioral correction (ownership). Failure modes include overfitting to small datasets or misalignment of ownership incentives with true value. These operators are embedded within a larger system of state transitions in GSE, where salary changes trigger lineup shifts and strategic re-evaluations.
